subject: Information Theory
title: Syndrome Decoding
description: A fast breakdown of Syndrome Decoding for builders.

hook.text: You receive a codeword with a possible error. Multiply by a check matrix. The result—the syndrome—reveals the fault.

buildup.text: Every linear code has a parity-check matrix H. Multiplying the received word by H gives the syndrome vector.

discovery.text: If the syndrome is zero, no error. If nonzero, the syndrome matches a column of H—pointing to the error position.

twist.text: For multiple errors, the syndrome identifies the most likely error pattern. Decoding becomes a lookup operation.

climax.text: Syndrome decoding turns error correction from guesswork into linear algebra. Fast, systematic, and provably optimal.

punchline.text: Multiply, check, fix. Algebra does the heavy lifting.

quiz.question: What does a nonzero syndrome indicate?
options: An error occurred and the syndrome identifies it
